d.d: To hit (someone or something) hard, especially with a flat implement or a stick; to thrash, to whack.
To drive or force (someone or something) by, or as if by, beating or hitting; to knock.
To pack (people or things) closely together; to cram.
An act of hitting hard, especially with a flat implement or a stick; a whack; also, a powerful stroke involved in such hitting; a blow, a strike.
A dull or heavy slapping sound.
Used to represent the dull or heavy sound of someone or something being hit or slapped.
Placed or situated across something else; cross, oblique, transverse.
To cause to fail; to frustrate, to prevent.
d.x: Our plans for a picnic were thwarted by the thunderstorm.

d.d: A seat across a boat on which a rower may sit.
d.x: The fisherman sat on the aft thwart to row.

d.d: A brace, perpendicular to the keel, that helps maintain the beam (“breadth”) of a marine vessel against external water pressure and that may serve to support the rail.
d.x: A well-made dugout canoe rarely needs a thwart.
